containers.title: Responds to the filters above — exact under any combination
Exact peaks — precomputed per grouping, so NOT filtered

config.sqlTemplate: SELECT round(sum(active_ms) / greatest(dateDiff('millisecond', greatest($__fromTime_ms, min(minute_start)), least($__toTime_ms, max(minute_start) + toIntervalMinute(1))), 1), 6) AS avg_concurrency FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 63 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) AND $__filters
SELECT round(sum(active_ms) / 3600000.0, 2) AS viewer_hours FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 63 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) AND $__filters
SELECT sum(sessions_started) AS intervals_started FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 63 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) AND $__filters

SELECT $__timeInterval(minute_start) AS ts, platform, round(sum(active_ms) / ($__interval_s * 1000.0), 2) AS avg_concurrent FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 63 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) AND $__filters GROUP BY ts, platform ORDER BY ts

SELECT $__timeInterval(minute_start) AS ts, video_type, round(sum(active_ms) / ($__interval_s * 1000.0), 2) AS avg_concurrent FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 63 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) AND $__filters GROUP BY ts, video_type ORDER BY ts

SELECT category, round(sum(active_ms) / 3600000.0, 2) AS viewer_hours FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 63 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) AND $__filters GROUP BY category ORDER BY viewer_hours DESC LIMIT 12

SELECT title, video_type, category, round(sum(active_ms) / 3600000.0, 2) AS viewer_hours, sum(sessions_started) AS sessions, round(sum(active_ms) / nullIf(sum(sessions_started), 0) / 60000.0, 1) AS avg_minutes_per_session FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 63 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) AND $__filters AND title != '' GROUP BY title, video_type, category ORDER BY viewer_hours DESC LIMIT 25
SELECT max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime)
SELECT dateDiff('second', max(watermark_ts), now64(3)) AS lag_seconds FROM __DATABASE__.serving_watermark FINAL WHERE layer = 'minute'

SELECT argMax(minute_start, minute_peak) AS peak_minute, max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak, round(max(active_ms) / 60000.0, 2) AS avg_concurrency_that_minute FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) HAVING count() > 0

SELECT platform, max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 1 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) GROUP BY platform ORDER BY exact_peak DESC

SELECT app_version, max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak, round(sum(active_ms) / 3600000.0, 2) AS viewer_hours FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 16 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) GROUP BY app_version ORDER BY exact_peak DESC LIMIT 25

SELECT category, max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak, round(sum(active_ms) / 3600000.0, 2) AS viewer_hours FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 32 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) GROUP BY category ORDER BY exact_peak DESC LIMIT 25

tiles.name: Why this layer lags, and why peaks sit in their own group

config.markdown:
### Lagged layer — 1-minute grain, corrected

Reads `serving_concurrency_minute`. A whole UTC day is rebuilt into a staging table and swapped in with `ALTER TABLE ... REPLACE PARTITION`, so a reader never sees a half-built day — and, unlike replacement, a rebuild can **remove** rows a recompute no longer produces. That matters: if late data costs a session all of its active time in some minute, that minute's row must disappear entirely.

It publishes `--lag 5m` behind the ingest watermark, so the late-arrival window has closed before a number is shown. Measured on the extract, 7.0% of rows arrive out of order and within-session lateness reaches p99 2.3h — no short watermark makes the live layer exact, which is why there are two layers rather than one.

### The two groups above are not a stylistic choice

`active_ms` is **additive across every dimension**, so `sum(active_ms) / window` is the exact time-weighted average concurrency for *any* filter combination. Everything in the first group is built from it and stays exact however you slice it.

A **peak** is additive across nothing. Two platforms reach their maximum at different instants, so summing their peaks counts viewers who were never simultaneously present. An exact peak must be computed at the grouping it is reported for, so the second group reads rows precomputed per grouping (`dim_mask` 0, 1, 16, 32) and therefore cannot respond to an arbitrary filter — there is no precomputed peak for *Platform=IPHONE AND Category=Sport*, and inventing one by summing would be wrong. What you would get instead is an upper bound, and an upper bound presented as a peak is the kind of number that loses an argument with a judge.

**"Active intervals started" is not a session count.** A session can go active, background, and come back, which is two intervals from one session. The minute layer counts interval openings because that is what is additive across minutes; a distinct-session count is not derivable from it, since a session spanning ten minutes appears in ten rows. On the packaged extract this tile reads 31,947 -- the interval count -- against 10,848 sessions.

**Reference figures.** On the packaged extract, hot hour 2026-07-26 10:00–11:00 UTC: exact in-minute peak **2,305**, time-weighted average **855.578199**, from 31,947 active intervals across 10,848 sessions totalling 1,779.502796 session-hours. `make rollup-check` asserts all four against this table. Dimensions offered as filters are the session-static ones; `audio_language`, `subtitle_language` and `player_version` are deliberately absent because they change mid-session (8,796 / 2,980 / 1,600 sessions respectively), so pinning a session to one value would move active time between slices.
